title: Isolation of murine large intestinal crypt cell populations with flow sorting
protocol: Identify mice to be used.
Prepare dissociation solution by mixing 160 mL of PBS, 160 µL of 1000x Rock Inhibitor (final concentration is 10 µM), and 800 µL of 0.4 M EDTA (final concentration is 2 mM).
Aliquot the dissociation solution into eight conical tubes in 20 mL portions.
Label five 50 mL conical tubes for each mouse with recommended labels: M#X - 100f #1; M#X - 100f #2; M#X - 40f #1; M#X - 40f #2, where X is the mouse ID.
Label four petri dishes for each mouse with the mouse ID and number.
Pour half full of cold PBS into labeled petri dishes.
Sacrifice mice immediately before proceeding to dissection.
Pin mouse on dissection tray.
Spray abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Make incision to open peritoneal cavity.
Gently scoop out the small intestine to the left side.
Cut through the pelvis just to the right of the rectum.
Find the rectum and cut at the end near the junction with the skin, avoiding blood vessels.
Cut the small intestine where it meets the cecum.
Gently tug the top of the colon; if correctly cut at the rectum, it will pull free with minimal mesentery tissue.
Place the colon in chilled PBS on an ice petri dish.
Snip off the tip of the cecum pouch.
Fill a 10 mL syringe attached to a popper needle with cold PBS and gently flush out the cecum to remove fecal matter.
Refill the syringe as needed and continue expelling PBS while threading the popper needle through the colon.
Expel all remaining PBS once the entire colon is threaded on the popper needle.
Place one point of dissecting scissors in the opening of the popper needle.
Use forceps to pull the intestine off the popper needle, cutting and linearizing as you pull the intestine towards you.
Keep linearized colon in PBS while proceeding with other colons.
Rinse colon by swirling in clean PBS until a majority of fecal material is removed.
Place clean linearized colons in dissociation solution #1 and place at a slow rotation for 30 min at 4 °C.
Remove colon tissue from dissociation solution #1.
Cut tissue into small ~3-5 mm pieces using forceps to dangle the tissue above dissociation tube #2 with edge of tissue resting on tube rim to pull taut and cutting with scissors.
Make sure all pieces are immersed in the dissociation solution #2.
Place back on rotator at 4 °C for an additional 30 min rotation.
Adjust settings to 500 xg, 5 min, 4 °C, and decrease deceleration speed to low setting.
Collect conical tubes after the 30 min dissociation step (total of 1 hour) and shake very aggressively for 3 minutes.
Pour suspension through a 100 µm filter into a new conical tube.
Rinse the filter with cold PBS, collecting up to 40-50 mL total volume.
Collect tissue chunks trapped in the filter and return them to the dissociation tube.
Re-use this filter for the next sample's 100 µm filtration step.
Add approximately 20 mL of PBS to the dissociation tube containing tissue chunks and store it on ice.
Repeat steps involving pouring through a 100 µm filter, rinsing, collecting tissue, and adding PBS for all samples.
Centrifuge all 100 µm filter #1 tubes at 500 xg, 5 min, 4 °C with decreased deceleration speed.
Manually shake the tissue in dissociation solution tubes (now containing 20 mL of PBS) again for 3 minutes rapidly.
Filter through 100 µm filter into a new tube.
Rinse with PBS for a final volume of ~40-50 mL.
Gently pour off supernatant from the 100 µm filter #1 tube and resuspend in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Mix well with a pipet to achieve a homogenous suspension.
Filter the suspension through a 40 µm filter into a new tube (40 µm filter #1 tube).
Rinse the filter with PBS filling to 50 mL.
Repeat step using the suspension from the second shake (100 µm filter #2 tubes) and filter into 40 µm filter #2 tube.
Centrifuge the suspension in both 40 µm filter tubes (#1 and #2) at 500 xg, 5 min, 4 °C, with a decreased deceleration speed to protect cell viability.
Prepare DNAse in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube by mixing 20 µL of 10x buffer (contains MgCl), 40 µL DNAse I, and 140 µL water.
Gently pour off supernatant from the 40 µm filter tubes and resuspend each cell pellet in ~1 mL of FACS buffer.
Transfer the suspension into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes (if you end up with a larger volume, it is okay to use additional tubes).
Centrifuge at 1,000 xg for 5-10 minutes at 4 °C with a soft stop setting.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant from all tubes using a pipet.
Dispense 500 μL of FACS buffer to each tube.
If more than one tube was collected per sample, merge the contents into one tube with 500 μL FACS buffer total.
Add 50 μL of DNAse and mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down 5-10 times with a P-1000 pipet.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Collect the cells by centrifugation.
Remove supernatant carefully after centrifugation.
Resuspend cell pellets in a total of ~500 μL of FACS buffer.
Add CD117 (cKit) antibody – APC-Cy7 to each tube at a ratio of 1:100, amounting to 5 μL per tube.
Add CD326 (Epcam) antibody – eFluor450 to each tube at a ratio of 1:100, amounting to 5 μL per tube.
Add CD44 antibody – PerCP-Cy5 to the cell suspensions.
Mix 5 μL of antibody for CD24 with a dilution of [1:200].
Mix 2.5 μL of antibody for CD31 with a dilution of [1:200].
Mix 2.5 μL of antibody for CD45 with a dilution of [1:200].
Combine 20 μL each of cKit, Epcam, and CD44.
Combine 10 μL each of CD24, CD31, and CD45.
Vortex the mixture briefly.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Collect cells by centrifugation at 1,000 x g for 5-10 minutes at 4 °C with a soft stop setting.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of fresh FACS buffer to the cell pellet, resuspend thoroughly, and centrifuge again.
Remove the supernatant after washing.
Resuspend each cell suspension in approximately 500 µL to 1 mL of fresh FACS buffer into a 5 mL round-bottom tube labeled 'To Sort'.
Add Live/Dead Aqua dye at a concentration of 1 µL per 1 mL of cell suspension, wrap the tube in foil, and incubate at room temperature for about 2 minutes.
Incubate samples for an additional 5-10 minutes before running on FACS but store them on ice in the meantime.
Store all samples on ice and protect from light until sorting is required.
Prepare tubes or reagents for collection if sorting will be followed by RNA isolation.
Store collection tubes on ice/chilled prior to, during, and after sorting.
Sort populations of live cells according to the provided gating schema.
Use BD FACS Aria Fusion with a 100 μm nozzle (20 PSI) for cell sorting.
